newsitem.title: USA: Disney unit readies launch of online service.
newsitem.headline: Disney unit readies launch of online service.

text.p: Disney Online, the Internet unit of entertainment giant Walt Disney Co, is planning to launch a subscriber-based online service in the spring of 1997, the Internet news service C/Net reported on Tuesday.
Currently, Disney Online is responsible for developing content and running Disney's three sites on the World Wide Web, Disney.com, family.com and movie.com.
Those three sites offer information on the company's theme parks, merchandise, movies, television shows and also provide educational content and activities for children.

A Disney online service, like one currently offered by America Online Inc or CompuServe Corp, might include e-mail, chat rooms, bulletin board listings and an Internet connection, according to C/Net's report.
C/Net said Disney is mulling different pricing schemes that would start at $5.00 and run up to $20.00 per month.

A spokeswoman for Disney Online declined to comment on the report, but since the company brought in Jake Winebaum from its magazine publishing wing in August 1995 to run Disney Online, analysts have expected Disney to offer a subscriber online service. C/Net, a unit of CNET Inc, operates a news service on the Internet focused on Net-related companies and news.
